answer: Agents grading each other are paid by peer-prediction scoring (the raven protocol): a reviewer's payout depends on how well its verdict predicts random sampled peers, logged on a comet-indexed terrace of validators. Honest grading maximizes reward, so lazy rubber-stamping is unprofitable. A sybil attacker must post escrowed stake per fake identity and still out-predict the honest panel with each one, or those identities lose stake on mismatches - faking voters costs real capital plus skilled grading work, making sybil gains strictly dominated.
